catalog_quote: TT is a tonal language. Syllables have H[igh], L[ow], F[alling], or R[ising] tone. F is the same as <HL>, and R is equivalent to <LH>, where angled brackets indicate syllabic groupings. ... In addition to lexical tones on noun, verb, and other stems, there are some word-internal grammatical tone overlays, and other overlays affecting words that are controlled by the morphosyntactic context. As a result, the lexical tones are often completely overwritten ... [3.7.1] Each noun, adjective, numeral, verb, and other lexical stem has a lexical tone contour. audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote verified verbatim in the held 2010 draft at the stated sections. The deciding source is the language's only reference grammar, by its fieldworker; Glottolog's three descriptive refs are all versions of it. The 2015 published edition (open, CC-BY) was downloaded and read at the same sections: it restates that TT is a tonal language with syllabic H/L/<HL>/<LH> tones, lexical stem melodies (all-L excluded) and grammatical/tonosyntactic overlays, with the only rhythmic material being the morphologically conditioned strong/weak vowel-reduction grid in verb stems (sec. 3.2.2), explicitly not a stress system. Classification 'tonal, no word stress described' stands. Only action: re-point the citation/locator to Heath 2015 (DOI 10.17617/2.2157088, pp. 5, 15-16, 54-55) instead of the the Internet Archive 2010 draft; no reclassification. Caveat: web search for independent prosody/instrumental studies could not be run

sources.quote: 'TT is a tonal language. Syllables have H[igh], L[ow], falling <HL>, or rising <LH> tone. ... In addition to lexical tones on noun, verb, and other stems, there are some word-internal grammatical tone overlays, and other overlays affecting words that are controlled by the morphosyntactic context.' Sec. 3.7.1: 'Each noun, adjective, numeral, verb, or other stem has a lexical tone melody. ... The one theoretically possible tone pattern that is excluded as a possible lexical melody is all-low /L/. That is, every stem has at least one H-tone component.' Sec. 3.2.2 keeps the verb-stem strong/weak m
